per_case.playbook: Isolate 192.168.100.46 from the network to stop the ongoing brute-force/service abuse against 192.168.100.5:80. Investigate the host for compromise (malware, credential theft, unauthorized automation). Block or rate-limit outbound connections to 192.168.100.5. Review 192.168.100.5 for signs of successful breach. Correlate with endpoint telemetry once the host is quarantined.

Isolate 192.168.100.5 from the network immediately. Preserve forensic evidence (memory dump, disk image, flow logs). Malware-scan the host, terminate C2/beacon channels, and investigate lateral movement toward 192.168.100.3 and the 5 beaconing internal hosts. Block outbound flows to 192.168.100.3 and review the beaconing internal hosts for compromise.

No action required. Mark the FLOW-002 alert as a false positive. If desired, tune the detection rule to account for large-payload, long-duration flows and bidirectional service relationships to reduce future false positives.

ISOLATE_HOST — Isolate 192.168.100.7 from the network immediately. Investigate for malware/rootkits and the beacon to 192.168.100.3:565 (internal C2). Preserve forensic images, perform memory/disk forensics, identify the initial access vector, and block outbound traffic to 192.168.100.3. Also hunt for other hosts beaconing to 192.168.100.3.

BLOCK the external IP 162.208.20.178 at the perimeter firewall/egress filter. Concurrently investigate the 6 internal source hosts (especially 192.168.10.5 with 3,625 flows) for malware/compromise and isolate them, as they are the compromised endpoints beaconing to this C2. Add the IP to threat intelligence blocklists and monitor for any new beaconing attempts to alternate C2 addresses.

BLOCK the external C2 IP 178.255.83.1 at the perimeter firewall (inbound and outbound). Concurrently investigate the 12 internal source hosts (192.168.10.5, .8, .9, .12, .14, .15, .16, .17, .19, .25, .50, .51) for malware and credential compromise, as they are the compromised endpoints beaconing outbound. Isolate those hosts and initiate endpoint remediation.
No action required. The target is operating as a benign DNS server. Confirm 192.168.10.1 is an authorized DNS resolver and continue normal monitoring. No need to isolate host or block any IP.

per_case.playbook: No action required. Dismiss the FLOW-002 alert as a false positive. Optionally tune the flow sensor to exclude internal DNS (port 53/UDP) resolver traffic from brute-force/service-abuse heuristics, since high-volume queries to a trusted internal resolver are normal client behavior.

BLOCK the external IP 205.174.165.73 at the perimeter firewall (inbound and outbound) and add it to the threat intelligence blocklist. Simultaneously investigate the 6 internal source hosts (192.168.10.5, .8, .9, .14, .15, .25) for malware and consider isolating them, as they are the compromised beacon senders. Preserve the network_traffic records as evidence for the incident response case.

BLOCK the external C2 IP 23.50.75.27 at the perimeter firewall/egress filter. Since the internal hosts (192.168.10.5, .8, .9, .12, .14, .15, .16, .17, .19, .25, .51) are the compromised beaconing sources, initiate host investigation/remediation on those endpoints and block outbound connections to 23.50.75.27 to sever the C2 channel.

Block outbound traffic to 23.61.187.27 at the perimeter firewall. Investigate the 12 internal source hosts for malware/compromise and remediate. Correlate with endpoint telemetry to identify the initial access vector. Maintain the block indefinitely as this is a confirmed C2 infrastructure IP.

BLOCK the external C2 IP 72.167.239.239 at the perimeter firewall/egress filtering immediately. In parallel, isolate and forensically image the 11 internal hosts (192.168.10.5, 8, 9, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 25, 51) that are beaconing to it, as they are the compromised trojanized endpoints. Hunt for the malware family responsible, block the domain/IP at DNS and proxy layers, and review for additional C2 channels.

No immediate blocking or isolation action. Retain the alert for review but do not block 72.21.91.29 or isolate hosts. Recommend monitoring the internal hosts (192.168.10.x) and destination for a shift toward a beaconing signature (regular intervals, consistent small payloads, off-standard ports). If flows later consolidate into equal-size periodic check-ins, escalate to BLOCK_IP for 72.21.91.29 and ISOLATE_HOST for the sending hosts.
